example: Circle: choose Circle, enter Radius 10. Step 1: area = π × 10² = 3.14159 × 100 = 314.16 square units. Step 2: circumference = 2 × π × 10 = 62.83 units. Rectangle: choose Rectangle, enter Length 10 and Width 5. Area = 10 × 5 = 50 square units; perimeter = 2 × (10 + 5) = 30 units. Triangle: choose Triangle, enter Base 10 and Height 5. Area = ½ × 10 × 5 = 25 square units. Final results: circle 314.16, rectangle 50, triangle 25 square units. Trapezoid: choose Trapezoid, enter a = 10, b = 6, height (c) = 4. Area = ½ × (10 + 6) × 4 = 32 square units.

faqs.a: Five shapes: Square, Rectangle, Triangle, Circle, and Trapezoid. Choose the shape first, then enter its dimensions.
Enter the side length once. Area = side × side and perimeter = 4 × side.
faqs.q: How do I calculate a square?

faqs.a: Enter the two parallel sides in fields (a) and (b), then enter the height — the distance between the two parallel sides — in field (c). Area = ½ × (a + b) × height.
faqs.q: What do I enter for a trapezoid?

faqs.a: The tool uses the units you enter, so keep them consistent — metres with metres, centimetres with centimetres — and the area comes out in square units of the same kind.
faqs.q: Are the results in square metres?

formula: Square: area = side², perimeter = 4 × side. Rectangle: area = length × width, perimeter = 2 × (length + width). Triangle: area = ½ × base × height. Circle: area = π × radius², circumference = 2 × π × radius. Trapezoid: area = ½ × (side a + side b) × height (c), where a and b are the two parallel sides and c is the height between them.
howTo: Choose the shape in the Shape dropdown: Square, Rectangle, Triangle, Circle, or Trapezoid.
Enter the first dimension in the Side / Length / Radius (a) field, for example 10.
Enter the second dimension in the Width / Height / Top-Width (b) field when the shape needs one.
For a trapezoid, also enter the height — the distance between the two parallel sides — in the Height (c) field.
Tap Calculate to see the area.
Read the perimeter or circumference shown under the result.
intro: The Area Calculator works out the area and perimeter of squares, rectangles, triangles, circles, and trapezoids from their dimensions.
mistakes: Entering the diameter instead of the radius for a circle, which makes the area four times too large.
Mixing units, such as length in metres and width in centimetres.
Using the slant side of a triangle as its height.
Forgetting that area is in square units while perimeter is in plain units.
tips: Measure twice before calculating — a wrong length gives a wrong area no matter how good the maths is.
For a room, multiply length by width in metres to get the floor area in square metres.
For a circle, measure across the middle and halve it to get the radius.
Keep all measurements in the same unit before entering them.
uses: It is used to find the area of a floor, plot, wall, or garden, and the perimeter or circumference, for painting, flooring, fencing, and school geometry.
